push in - improper fractions, mixed fractions

began the lesson focusing on main idea and key details. However, after monitoring student understanding, it became clear that the scholars were not yet secure with identifying the main idea. I adjusted the lesson in the moment and narrowed the focus to main idea only.

To support their understanding, I introduced a visual scaffold using three labeled boxes: Too Small, Too Big, and Just Right. This helped students distinguish between a single detail (too small), the general topic (too big), and a complete main idea that includes all key examples (just right).

This adjustment allowed both scholars to correctly identify the main idea by the end of the lesson.
